title: Spec checking
description: Running the checks, adding new ones, reviewing what they find, keeping every level of the spec a useful size, and keeping every change checked.

title: Spec reading
description: Product, domain and record pages: coverage, obligation kinds and test states, finding a record and following its links.

title: Workspace navigation
description: One address per record, its Graph, ERD and Trace stages behind floating panels, the wiki card, the nav, quick find and keyboard shortcuts.

title: Graph exploration
description: Walking the model as a left-to-right graph with folder-like groups.

title: Workspace tabs
description: Several places open at once, each a tab with its own address and history: opening, activating, cycling, duplicating and closing them.

title: Interface design
description: What a flow reaches: views and their requirements, endpoints and their API requirements, integrations and the UI components that draw the views.

title: View design
description: Keeping a view, its view requirements and its view tests.

title: Endpoint design
description: Keeping an endpoint, its API requirements, its handler and its endpoint tests.

title: Integration design
description: Keeping an integration, its adapter and its integration tests.

title: Domain modeling
description: A product split into domains by capability: adding, changing and moving its domains and their capabilities.

title: Domain upkeep
description: Removing domains and capabilities, and keeping the terms and repositories of a domain.

title: Domain services
description: Keeping a domain's domain services, the services that implement them and their tests.

title: Aggregates and their parts
description: Keeping an aggregate with its entities and their data models.

title: Domain behavior
description: Keeping commands and their handlers, policies, the event handlers that carry them out and policy tests.

title: Specifications and predicates
description: Keeping specifications with their predicates and tests.

title: Value objects
description: Keeping value objects with their constraints, value types and constraint tests.

title: Read models
description: Keeping read models with their queries and query handlers.

title: Domain events
description: Keeping domain events with their event types.

title: Invariants and their rules
description: Keeping an aggregate's invariants with the rules that hold them and their invariant tests.

title: Projections and readers
description: Keeping the projections that fill read models and the readers that read them.

title: Storage requirements
description: Keeping what an aggregate or read model needs of its storage, with the storage requirement tests.

title: Workbench
description: Panels, themes, phones, stability and accessibility: what every view stands on.

title: Live loading
description: Loading a workspace from the data files, from code or a view, fast enough to reload live, and views that follow the data files as they change.

title: Desktop hosting
description: Opening products in windows, iterating on Lathe in the shell with hot reload, using Lathe from the native menus, a window that looks like part of Lathe, and an app that feels native on a Mac.

title: Repo setup
description: Setting Lathe up in a product's repo, moving a product to a new Lathe, and starting the plugin's tools there.

title: Chat with Claude
description: Talking with the Owner's own Claude Code beside the stage: sending messages, answering prompts, choosing how it works, reviewing and undoing what it changed.

title: Dictation
description: Speaking a message to the chat: listening, the wake phrase and Quick mode.

title: Claude sign-in
description: Signing the chat's agent in and out of its Claude account from the product.

title: Product customization
description: The product itself, its roles and interfaces, the kinds and relations it declares and their records, the stages and order of kinds, the reference that shows them, and merging two branches' changes to its data.

title: Discovery
description: Who the product is for and why: its business outcomes, each with its measure and target, its roles, the interfaces they work through and its open questions.

title: Journeys
description: The journeys that reach a product's business outcomes: their steps and handoffs, the use cases the steps carry out and the journey tests that prove them.

title: Technical specification
description: How the product is run and built: its entry points and its tooling.

title: Standards
description: The rules the product's code and models follow: its standards, their rules and the standard rule tests that prove them.

title: Tables and data stores
description: Where the product keeps its records: its data stores, and the tables in them with their keys.

title: Coverage measurement
description: How much of each obligation is designed, built and proved, what is proved only by tests not automated yet, and what is still missing.

title: Test evidence
description: How a test is run, and how its file names it.

title: Coverage reporting
description: Coverage, tests by state, the patterns a domain owes and each record's traces, as the app shows them.

title: Test planning
description: The tests that prove each record: the test of its kind, how it runs, and the test data sets tests start from.

title: Use case writing
description: Use cases with their requirements, flows and tests, and the patterns they follow.

title: Requirement writing
description: Keeping a use case's UC requirements and the use case tests that prove them.

title: Flow writing
description: Keeping a use case's flow, its steps and its flow test.

title: Pattern writing
description: Keeping a pattern, its rules and rule tests, and its slots.
